transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Lately I feel this heavy, empty mood all the time, like I’m weighed down and can’t shake it no matter what I do. It's just really exhausting, and I don't know how to get past it.
Have you been feeling this way consistently for at least two years, or is this a distinct period of low mood that began more recently?

No, it hasn't been quite two years, but it's been going on for about a year and a half now. It really started to snowball after I took on a lot of extra night shifts at work to help my parents with rent. Since then, this heavy, empty feeling has been there pretty much every single day.
Have you experienced similar periods of this low mood in the past, perhaps years ago, or is this the first time you have ever felt this way?

No, this is the first time I've ever felt this way. Before I started working those extra night shifts about a year and a half ago, I never had periods of this heavy, empty mood. It's completely new to me.
During these past 18 months, have there been times when your mood felt significantly worse, accompanied by symptoms like changes in appetite, sleep, or a loss of interest in almost all activities?

Yes, for a little over a year now, that empty feeling has been constant and I've completely lost interest in painting murals and playing soccer. My appetite also totally vanished, and I've lost so much weight that my pants are hanging off me.
Are you able to carry out your daily work and household responsibilities, or have your symptoms become so severe that you are unable to function at all?

It's gotten really hard to function, and I went from being a reliable aide to calling out of shifts and getting written up for making mistakes. At home, I've completely let things like laundry, cleaning, and cooking slide, and I barely even see my friends anymore. It just feels like everything is falling apart.
Have you noticed any physical slowing of your movements or speech, or have you experienced any feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt that make it difficult for you to think or concentrate?

Yes, people at work and home keep telling me I move and speak in slow motion, and just walking down the hall feels like dragging a hundred-pound backpack. My head is also so foggy that basic things like charting or even choosing what to cook completely overwhelm me. I just get stuck staring, completely unable to make a simple decision.
Have you been experiencing any unusual thoughts, such as hearing voices that others don't hear, or feeling as though your thoughts are being controlled or broadcast to others?

I don't hear any voices, but I've been having some really anxious thoughts lately that I can't shake. I feel like the cameras on the psychiatric unit and even the mirrors at home are watching me specifically, like they're part of an experiment to read and record my thoughts. Everyone tells me it isn't true, but it feels so real to me and it's really unsettling.

latest_inference.note: The patient's report of delusional beliefs (feeling watched by cameras and mirrors as part of an experiment) alongside severe depressive symptoms, psychomotor retardation, and functional impairment indicates the presence of psychotic features. This shifts the diagnosis from F32.2 (severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms) to F32.3 (severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a major depressive episode of 18 months duration characterized by severe vegetative symptoms (weight loss, psychomotor retardation), cognitive impairment, and functional decline. Crucially, the patient exhibits mood-congruent delusions (persecutory/paranoid ideas regarding being watched/recorded) during the depressive episode, meeting criteria for major depressive disorder with psychotic features.
